sentences.text:
1. Heard Mr. Mayur Kadam, learned Advocate for the Petitioners, Mr. Prasanna Malshe, learned APP for the Respondent/State and Mr. Jitendra Oak, learned Advocate for Respondent No.2.
2.

This Petition/Application under Article 226 of the Constitution of India and under Section 528 of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 is preferred by the Petitioners for quashing the FIR bearing 101 of 2024 registered at Kalyan Taluka Police Station, Thane Graming for the offences (911) WP-826.26.DOCX punishable under Sections 498A, 377, 506, 406 r/w 34 of the Indian Penal Code and the Chargesheet bearing No.77 of 2024, registered as Case No.RCC/416/2024), pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Kalyan 3.

sentences.text: He tenders the Photostat copy of Identity Card of Respondent No.2, which is taken on record and marked as "X-1" for identification.

5. Mr Mayur Kadam, learned Advocate for the Petitioners and Mr. Jitendra Oak, learned Advocate for the Respondent No.2, submit that the dispute pertaining to the impugned FIR and the consequent chargesheet is being resolved between the (911) WP-826.26.DOCX Petitioners and the Respondent No.2.
They submit that the Respondent No.2 has given no objection in her Affidavit dated 20 February 2026, original of which is filed in Criminal Writ Petition No.4790 of 2024.
The copy of the Affidavit dated 20 February 2026 is taken on record and marked as "X-2" for identification.
6. Respondent No. 2 states that the said Affidavit (X-2) is filed out of her own free will and without any pressure or coercion from any person.
She states that the contents of the Affidavit (X-2) are as per her say.
She reiterates her no objection for quashing of the criminal proceedings.

7. Ms. Shilpa Talhar, learned APP for the Respondent/State submits that the matrimonial disputes between the Petitioners and the Respondent No.2 being resolved and the Respondent No.2 having filed Affidavit (X-2) giving no objection for quashing the criminal proceedings, no purpose would be served in continuing with the criminal proceedings.
She however insists for imposition of costs.

(911) WP-826.26.DOCX 8. Mr. Mayur Kadam, learned Advocate for the Petitioners and Mr. Jitendra Oak, learned Advocate for the Respondent No.2, on instructions, submits that the Petitioners and Respondent No.2 shall deposit appropriate costs.

9. Considering the aforesaid circumstances, the nature of dispute, the matter being settled between the Petitioners and the Respondent No.2, the statement of Respondent No. 2 in the Affidavit (X-2)
and having regards to the pronouncements of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Gian Singh vs State Of Punjab1, Narinder Singh And Ors vs State Of Punjab And Anr2 and Parbatbhai Aahir @
Parbatbhai vs The State Of Gujarat3, there is no impediment in allowing this Application.
